Nilpotency-class distinct quiver witnesses share all off-diagonal Peirce dimensions. Four full enumerations independently check k=0..3 and maximal clique sizes for q=2,3; the proof, not the checks, establishes all q,n,k.

value.rationale: The natural problem asks what a full idempotent compatibility invariant recovers about a finite basic algebra. The theorem gives the complete all-arity answer in terms of explicit symmetric radical Peirce dimensions and shows this invariant forgets radical multiplication and orientation. Equal-dimensional nonisomorphic algebras whose radical squares differ have identical clique polynomials, a motivated structural obstruction to reconstruction not implied by knowing individual idempotent counts. Generality and witness make it more than a routine numerical census.
